record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: minimal weight of separable non-CDH manifolds
record.original_question: Is the cardinal invariant b the minimal possible weight of a separable non-countable-dense-homogeneous manifold; if not, is there a natural combinatorial characterization of that minimal weight?

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Is b the minimal weight of a separable, non-CDH manifold?
If not, is there (as Watson asks) a nice combinatorial characterization of the minimal weight of a separable, non-CDH manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A topological space $X$ is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D) = E$. The weight $w(X)$ of a topological space $X$ is the minimum cardinality of a base for its topology. A manifold here is a (Hausdorff) topological space in which every point has an open neighborhood homeomorphic to some Euclidean (or Hilbert-cube) chart; in particular separable manifolds of arbitrarily large weight are admitted (so the manifold need not be second countable).

Let $\mathfrak{b}$ denote the bounding number, i.e. the least cardinality of an unbounded family in $(\omega^{\omega}, \le^{*})$, where $f \le^{*} g$ means $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$.

Define
$$\mu = \min\{\, w(M) : M \text{ is a separable manifold that is not CDH}\,\}.$$

Questions.
(a) Is $\mu = \mathfrak{b}$?
(b) If not, is there a natural combinatorial characterization (in the sense of cardinal invariants of the continuum) of the cardinal $\mu$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was located. It is stated as an open problem in the survey on countable dense homogeneity, and subsequent web searches did not turn up any paper announcing that the minimal weight of a separable non-CDH manifold equals $\mathfrak{b}$ or providing a combinatorial characterization. The problem appears to remain open.
